preamble: The voiced alveolo-palatal fricative [ʑ] became the aspirated retroflex affricate [ʈʂʰ] in a subset of Mandarin words. The source is the Middle Chinese 船 initial, reconstructed as [ʑ] (Baxter zy-) by Baxter, Zhengzhang and Pulleyblank, whose values for 船 and 禪 reverse the traditional rime-table assignment. Most 船 words have Mandarin [ʂ] (see zh_palatal_to_sh_retroflex), but several level-tone words were devoiced as aspirated affricates, the regular Mandarin treatment of voiced obstruents in the level tone; the doublet 乘 chéng 'ride' (level) beside shèng 'vehicle' (departing) shows the split.

examples.note: The departing-tone reading zyingH 'vehicle' became shèng with [ʂ].

sources: Baxter, William H. (1992). A Handbook of Old Chinese Phonology. Mouton de Gruyter. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110857085
